tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has gathered a Qwen long-horizon agent report, an O-RAN benchmark, agentic-RL training papers, and AWS's SageMaker guide.
why_it_matters: Agent RL is now judged on cost and reliability: EnvSched and calibrated budgets (Oct 20) target rollout spend, while MiRL and CalibraRL target named failures. All are paper-reported results, not production evidence; the SageMaker guide remains the only managed-platform recipe.

beats.headline: Alibaba Qwen introduces QwenGyre for elastic RL on extra-long-horizon agents
beats.summary: Reported via MarkTechPost; targets agent tasks that run far longer than standard RL rollouts.

beats.headline: X-RIC benchmarks agentic RAN controllers for reinforcement learning
beats.summary: Targets O-RAN controllers rather than LLM post-training.

beats.headline: Agentic RL papers: rollout budgets, stateful environments, search-state awareness, credit assignment
beats.summary: Four arXiv papers on cutting rollout cost, extending RL beyond tool-centric settings, teaching search agents to assess their own state, and crediting individual decisions within an episode.

beats.headline: AWS multi-turn RL guide, plus stability, simulation, robustness and token-credit papers
beats.summary: A managed-platform recipe on SageMaker AI and four arXiv papers on rounding alignment, token credit, dialogue user simulation and robust RL.

beats.headline: Reliability turn: calibrated rewards, credit-assignment limits, error-targeted agent fixes
beats.summary: Oct 26: three arXiv papers aim RL at hallucination, when fine-grained credit hurts, and terminal-agent misbehavior.

beats.headline: EnvSched: environment-aware scheduling for rollout-efficient agent RL
beats.summary: Oct 27: rollout generation and verification cost becomes the target as executable environments scale.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
Does the SageMaker MTRL recipe carry from Wordle to tool-using agent tasks, and at what training cost?
Does twin-world credit assignment improve agent training on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Do MiRL's error-targeted fixes hold on terminal-agent tasks outside the paper's own benchmark?
Does EnvSched's scheduling gain hold on agent-RL benchmarks beyond the paper's own, and with which environment mixes?
take_for_builders: If you train tool-using agents, measure rollout cost per environment (EnvSched, calibrated budgets), log recurring failure modes for error-targeted RL (MiRL), and A/B fine-grained credit against episode-level reward; treat paper results as unreplicated until rerun on your own evals.

status.detail: A loose set of RL items; the newest aim at rollout cost, agent reliability and credit-assignment limits.
